To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a model for describing the technical environment of scientific research experiments is needed; (b) the model should be aligned with existing approaches to describe the research process; (c) the model should support the description of a variety of technical environments; and (d) the model should allow for a flexible description of the technical environment, while still being able to describe a large number of technical aspects.

the model we propose provides the necessary means to describe the context of scientific experiment processes, that this model is based on the use of ontologies and that it can be used for the purpose of re-usability and re-execution of e-Science experiment processes.

1) we have defined a model for describing the context of scientific experiments; 2) we have implemented a proof-of-concept application of the model; and 3) we have shown how the model relates to the Research Object concept.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how we can describe and model the context of an experiment, and how this can be used for reuse and reproducibility of scientific research.
the development of a model for describing the technical infrastructure of e-Science experiment processes.
the development of a model for describing and representing scientific experiments, with an emphasis on the technical infrastructure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is complementary to Research Objects, and can be used to describe the technical environment in a more detailed manner than the current Research Object specification.
Research Objects are a more comprehensive and flexible approach, but that they lack a formal model for describing the technical environment of the experiments.
we believe our model to provide a complementary perspective to Research Objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and evaluated a model for representing the technical context of an experiment, and that this model has a clear focus on the technical context, and can be used as a complement to other approaches for describing experiments, such as Research Objects.
we have developed an ontology that is able to describe the technical context in which experiments are executed.
our approach is a more fine-grained description of the infrastructure that is needed for a scientific experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can describe the context of an experiment, including the infrastructure it is executed in, in a formal, machine-interpretable way, allowing us to reason about the context of the experiment, and to compare experiments and their contexts.

the technical infrastructure of an e-Science experiment can be described using a number of ontologies, and that these ontologies are not specific to e-Science, but rather general purpose, and can thus be reused for other purposes.
we can use the model to describe the context of an experiment, which can be used to facilitate the re-usability and re-executability of the experiment.
